aspect: EXAMPLE - the finding, and its sex specificity
description: In HCHS/SOL, a sample of 3,848 Latinos across Cuban, Puerto Rican, Dominican, Mexican and South/Central American backgrounds found greater chronic and perceived stress significantly associated with allostatic load FOR MALES BUT NOT FEMALES, with ethnic background and nativity moderating the relationship for males.
energy_note: The stress-to-body pathway showed up in the men.
notes: The single most directly on-brief finding in this module: it is both about the body and specific to men.

description: An HCHS/SOL Sociocultural Ancillary Study analysis examined perceived discrimination against metabolic syndrome and its six components in 5,174 Hispanic/Latino adults, controlling for age, sex, income and acculturation. Related HCHS/SOL work found higher chronic stress burden associated with higher prevalence of coronary heart disease, hypertension and diabetes.
energy_note: It shows up as heart disease and diabetes.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the Boston Puerto Rican Health Study
description: 882 Puerto Rican adults were assessed for major lifetime and everyday perceived discrimination against allostatic load across 11 physiological components. The authors note perceived discrimination is associated with type 2 diabetes, heart disease and hypertension, and with inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress and a steeper cortisol awakening response.

aspect: THE HONEST GAP - the combined study does not exist
description: No single study was found combining perceived discrimination, cortisol and hypertension in Latino MEN within HCHS/SOL: the gendered allostatic load finding and the discrimination-cardiometabolic finding come from separate analyses. HCHS/SOL measures cortisol mainly via ancillary substudies. The chain is assembled from adjacent evidence and says so.
energy_note: Three findings that nobody has joined up.

aspect: Cortisol pathways are documented in Mexican-origin samples
description: Research in Mexican-origin adolescents and adults notes that discrimination experiences trigger cardiovascular activity and greater stress responses that over time contribute to allostatic load - so the mechanism is observed early in life.

aspect: It is the same finding as the Nigeria dataset, in a different body
description: assets/text/nigeria SOM-002 found domestic-stress appraisal predicting low back pain at OR 2.88 in rural Nigerian women. This file finds chronic stress predicting allostatic load in Latino men and not women. Two populations, two designs, the same mechanism - which is why both datasets carry a SOM category.
energy_note: Same mechanism, opposite sexes, two continents.
